articles.title: Far Right Gains Power
articles.author: Vijay Prashad
articles.content_excerpt: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. Brazil’s general election on 4 October delivered a severe warning to the Left. Flávio Bolsonaro, the presidential candidate of the Liberal Party (PL), finished ahead of President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, with approximately 47 per cent against 45 per cent. Neither secured a majority, sending them into a runoff on 25 October. More troubling than this narrow presidential gap was the advance of bolsonarismo through Congress. The election has strengthened a political movement whose ambitions extend beyond defeating Lula to reshaping the institutions that obstruct its exercise of power. articles.title: UE Hosts Belgian Trade Union Delegation in Pittsburgh
articles.content_excerpt: On October 3, UE hosted a delegation from the Belgian trade union FGTB. UE Secretary-Treasurer Andrew Dinkelaker and members of UE Local 667 joined the Belgian trade unionists at an Oktoberfest event in Pittsburgh, which raised money for Palestinians. The Belgian union delegation, members of the Belgian FGTB, was on a three-city tour (Minneapolis, Pittsburgh, and Chicago) to meet union leaders and other activists to discuss how they are fighting the far-right and fascism. During the Belgians’ visit, Dinkelaker gave a brief overview of UE’s history and rank-and-file structure. The Local 667 members spoke about their local’s ongoing campaign to boycott Israeli products at the East End Food Coop, where they work. The FGTB is a strong supporter of the Palestinian cause. articles.title: Western Region: Take Action to Defend Elections
articles.content_excerpt: “Our union is a powerful tool that we must utilize to attain a society and a world that is truly equitable and just for all,” declared Local 1186 Vice President Michele McCoy during the Western Region council meeting’s political action report. McCoy and Local 1107 President Kellye Allen were reporting on resolutions that their locals, both located in Wisconsin, had passed about defending labor and democratic rights in the upcoming midterm elections. McCoy also shared how members of her local have been collecting pledge cards in the local and in the community asking working people to pledge to vote for pro-worker candidates and to take action if the Trump Administration moves to interfere in the elections. What happens when cruelty becomes a governing philosophy? When political leaders celebrate violence, billionaires wield extraordinary influence over government, and institutions supposedly designed to defend democracy become instruments of repression? These questions were at the center of our recent conversation with political theorist Henry Giroux, whose latest LA Progressive essay, "The Politics of the Abyss: MAGA, Moral Rot, and the Struggle for the Future," examines what he considers the accelerating collapse of America's democratic and moral foundations. articles.title: Online Pornography Created the Model for Platform Capitalism
articles.author: Patricia Nilsson
articles.content_excerpt: Online pornography is often seen as a corner of the web that doesn’t bear much analysis. And yet it can hardly be ignored. Firstly, that’s because of the sheer size of the adult-content industry — a sector that in itself is worth around $97 billion annually worldwide and that, at peak times, commands 10 percent of all internet traffic. But more than that, a discussion of its inner workings sheds light on the mechanisms that govern the special kind of attention economy and platform capitalism that we are all wrapped up in. In the early 1950s, Senator Joseph McCarthy seemed to wield unchecked power. McCarthy was antisemitic, persecuted people he alleged were homosexual, and defended Nazi soldiers who had massacred American prisoners at Malmedy. His political practice was defined by false accusations and Congressional investigation of his political enemies, mostly advocates of left-of-center ideas. In 1954, his authority was shattered by facts from the mouths of Army counsel Joseph N. Welch and Senator Stuart Symington. Ethiopia and Eritrea simultaneously severed diplomatic ties on October 1st. It's a perilous situation. If one nation’s army crosses the other's border, it could draw in neighboring nations, creating a regional crisis from the Horn to the Gulf or, one might say, worsening the crisis that already exists with multiple civil and interstate wars. The entire world, knowledgeably or not, is invested in containing this conflict because of its potential to further destabilize the Red Sea, a major oil shipping channel, driving the price of gas even higher and triggering more inflation cascading upward. articles.title: Shawn Fain’s Slate Has Swept the UAW Elections
articles.author: Chris Brooks
articles.content_excerpt: Shawn Fain and the United UAW slate are headed toward a sweeping victory in the union’s internal elections for its International Executive Board. The results will not be finalized for some time, but the unofficial results are unequivocal: United Auto Workers members are overwhelmingly backing Fain and the militant direction he is taking the union. Voter turnout was low, about 10 percent of the total number of active and retired members, and appears to be on track for a lower total vote count than when the UAW held its first direct election of top union officers in 2022. Previously, officers were elected by delegates at the union’s annual convention, a system that helped entrench the ruling Administration Caucus in power for more than seven decades. articles.title: Eric Hobsbawm, Historian of Defeat
articles.author: Iker Itoiz Ciaurriz
articles.content_excerpt: Five years after the fall of the Berlin Wall, the communist historian Eric Hobsbawm published his best-selling history of the twentieth century, The Age of Extremes . The book presented a man coming to terms with the fate of the political project to which he had committed his adult life while trying to understand the twentieth century as a historical epoch. Though famous for its pessimism, the book, like the work of many left-wing authors in the 1990s, was also an opportunity to rethink what the project of the Left might become after the collapse of communism. In its final pages, Hobsbawm reflected darkly on the future. articles.title: Abdul El-Sayed Isn’t Backing Down on Medicare for All
articles.author: Matt Bruenig
articles.content_excerpt: The discourse around Abdul El-Sayed’s position on Medicare for All is mostly confused. Reading most of the reporting on the matter would lead one to believe that El-Sayed initially supported Medicare for All but now merely supports a “public option.” This is not really true under conventional meanings of the phrase “public option.” El-Sayed seems to be inviting this understanding for rhetorical effect, but all he has really done is drop his opposition to a type of duplicative insurance that nobody would ever want to buy. Conventional Public Options In the health insurance context, the phrase “public option” has typically referred to two types of arrangements: The government creates a health insurance plan and attempts to sell it in the employer and individual markets. articles.title: Anwar Shaikh’s Analysis of Capitalism Is Vital for the Left
articles.author: Howard Botwinick
articles.content_excerpt: Most economists assume that when workers with similar skills earn very different pay, something must be blocking normal competition. But for Howard Botwinick, capitalist competition itself creates those gaps. His book Persistent Inequalities: Wage Disparity under Capitalist Competition , first published in 1993 and reissued in 2017, shows how the everyday workings of capitalism split the working class into better- and worse-paid groups — no monopoly power required. Botwinick came to economics from organizing. Early on, he helped workers win a union at an electronics plant, only to watch the company shut the plant down rather than deal with them. articles.title: Pedro Sánchez Makes His Last Gamble
articles.author: Eoghan Gilmartin
articles.content_excerpt: Less than two weeks after a wave of housing protests broke out across Spain, on Monday center-left Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez called an early general election. Upending the country’s political agenda in just days, the protests created an opportunity for an embattled Sánchez to go to the polls on more favorable terms. He is now framing the election as a choice between his defense of the social majority and right-wing parties aligned with speculators and vulture funds. This was a remarkable turn of events, especially as Sánchez’s government had been in the firing line of housing protests just days before. articles.title: Unions Step Up to Meet the Moment
articles.content_excerpt: Featured image by Jared Rodriguez. Since taking office, Trump and MAGA forces have made considerable advances in implementing Project 2025 and consolidating authoritarian power—but many of these moves have proved unpopular and undermined their support. With Trump’s approval ratings dropping and elements of his coalition defecting, conditions look promising for pushing back MAGA in the midterm elections. But there are at least two sources of concern. With their support declining, the MAGA forces are likely to step up their efforts to interfere with the elections—doing everything from stopping people from voting to refusing to seat elected officials to unleashing violence. They pick up the car after you book, and then it’s just gone for a few days until it turns up at the other end. Most people never think about what actually happens behind the scenes. They probably should because that’s usually where things go right or wrong, and it almost always comes down to steps the customer never sees. Someone Checks the Car Over Before It Even Leaves Before anything gets loaded, a decent operator walks around the car and writes down its condition. Not a glance from three feet away; they’ll conduct an actual inspection. They take photos of every scratch, chip, and dent it already had before it left your driveway. After a fall, many people feel embarrassed and want to leave quickly. That reaction is understandable. But leaving without reporting what happened can make your claim harder to prove later. An incident report creates an early written record of the fall. It can show where the accident happened, when it happened, who was present, and what condition may have caused it. If the property owner later denies the incident or disputes the details, that report may become important. If you search “ slip and fall attorney near me ” and reach out to the right expert, they can review the report and compare it with photos, witness statements, medical records, and other evidence. Browse any car accessories store and half the products claim to be life-changing. Most of it is genuinely just noise, gimmicky gadgets that sound impressive in a product listing and end up sitting unused in a glovebox within a fortnight. However, it can’t be just any kind of phone mount. You’ll need something that’s top-notch quality, but not necessarily expensive.
